1. Start with the inspection records.

completion:
For each site/test that shows a test result, enter the value into the summary form. Make sure the value is correctly recorded, including the units of measure such as ppb (parts per billion) and mL/L (millilitres per litre).
3. Compare the test result with the compliance limit.
4. If the test result is greater than the compliance limit, take note of the site/name.
5. Declare the result a failure, and display it publicly on the summary report.

A municipal water system is declared to be non-compliant if:
- at any time a water sample analyzed in a certified laboratory has lead and/or copper above the Maximum Contaminant Level (MCL);
- at any time a water sample analyzed by a certified laboratory has nitrate or nitrite above the MCL.

There are two parts to reporting water samples:
